newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - May 20.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on May 20. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) has decided to cancel all campaigning in Jakarta on Tuesday for fear of further violence. Party supporters clashed with those of the ruling Golkar party and security officers on Saturday and Sunday.

The government has said the three parties contesting the May 29 general elections are allowed to continue campaigning despite rising tension and widespread fears of more violence. The government said campaigning will not be terminated until the end of the scheduled period on Friday.

The government has said factory workers who earn less than the minimum wage do not have to pay income tax. Starting April 1, the government increased minimum wages across the country to between 106,500 rupiah and 235,000 rupiah a month. They were between 96,000 rupiah and 220,500 rupiah a month before the rise.

The ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), Megawati Sukarnoputri, has denied allegations she has formed a coalition with the chairman of the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP), Ismail Hasan Metareum, to replace President Suharto.
